structure.overview: This case concerns a costs assessment following the Applicant's discontinuance of judicial review proceedings against the Respondent, Tataskweyak Cree Nation. The Respondent sought costs for work done on a motion to strike, but the court found that costs for the motion could not be fully awarded as the motion was neither abandoned nor decided before discontinuance. Ultimately, the court allowed partial costs totaling $1,075.20 payable by the Applicant to the Respondent.

sections.label: Filing and response to Bill of Costs
Assessment of costs related to motion to strike
Legal principles and equitable cost assessment

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: The Applicant discontinued their judicial review proceeding against the Respondents on April 12, 2022, prompting this costs assessment.

summaries.speaker: other
summaries.summary: Rules 402 and 412 of the Federal Courts Rules provide that costs are payable to a party against whom proceedings are discontinued or abandoned, and costs may be assessed upon filing a notice of discontinuance.

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: In absence of specific court direction, costs will be assessed under Rule 407 of the FCR, which mandates party-and-party costs per Tariff B, column III.

summaries.speaker: evidence
summaries.summary: On April 20, 2022, the Respondent Tataskweyak Cree Nation filed a Bill of Costs and covering letter initiating their request for cost assessment.

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: Tataskweyak Cree Nation will be referred to as the Respondent in these Reasons.

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: A direction was issued on April 25, 2022, for filing additional documents, but no further documents were filed; only the Respondent's Bill of Costs is before the court.

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: The Applicant did not respond to the Respondent's Bill of Costs, leaving it substantially unopposed; the court cites Dahl v Canada on handling unopposed bills.
idea_list: Dahl v Canada guidance on unopposed bills

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: The court cites Carlile v Canada emphasizing that Taxing Officers must balance not burdening unsuccessful litigants with costs and not denying indemnification to successful litigants with real costs incurred.

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: Despite no response from the Applicant, the Assessment Officer must ensure allowed costs are necessary and reasonable, reviewing all relevant materials accordingly.

summaries.speaker: evidence
summaries.summary: The Respondent claims 17 units for assessable services totaling $3,046.00 inclusive of taxes.

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: The court allows 1 unit for Item 25 and 3 units for Item 26 as necessary and reasonable; Items 5, 13(a), and 15 require further assessment.

summaries.speaker: evidence
summaries.summary: The Respondent claims 5 units for Item 5, 3 units for Item 13(a), and 5 units for Item 15, all related to the motion to strike the Applicant's judicial review application.

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: Rule 402 states a party against whom a proceeding is discontinued is entitled to costs; the Respondent's claims relate to a motion to strike filed April 8, 2022.

summaries.speaker: other
summaries.summary: Rule 411 provides that costs for an abandoned motion may be assessed upon filing a notice of abandonment or related documents.

summaries.speaker: other
summaries.summary: Rule 370 defines abandonment of a motion by serving a notice or failing to appear at the hearing, which is deemed abandonment.

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: The Respondent did not abandon their motion; the Applicant discontinued the proceeding before the motion was heard, so no court decision awarded costs for the motion.

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: The court cites Canada v Uzoni confirming that if a court order is silent on costs, no costs are awarded for the motion.

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: The Assessment Officer lacks authority to allow claims under Items 5, 13(a), and 15 since the motion was not abandoned and no court awarded costs; only Item 5 was accurately submitted but still disallowed.

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: Though Tursunbayev and Uzoni guide silent cost decisions, they don't address motions not disposed or abandoned when proceedings are discontinued; some indemnification may be possible depending on facts.

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: The Respondent filed the motion record April 8, 2022; the Applicant discontinued the proceeding April 12, 2022; the Respondent did considerable work on the motion and written representations.

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: The court supports some indemnification for the Respondent's work on the motion, citing Mitchell v Canada favoring positive application of costs provisions.

summaries.speaker: other
summaries.summary: Rule 3 of the FCR requires rules to be interpreted to secure just, expeditious, and least expensive determinations.

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: Applying Mitchell, Carlile, and Rule 3, the court allows 2 units under Item 27 for the motion work, considering factors under Rule 400(3) for equitable cost assessment.

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: A total of 6 units are allowed for the Respondent's assessable services, totaling $1,075.20 inclusive of taxes.

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: The Respondent did not claim any disbursements.

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: The Respondent's Bill of Costs is allowed in the amount of $1,075.20 payable by the Applicant; a Certificate of Assessment will be issued.
